title: Treat low-readiness days as part of the training picture
summary: If reaction quality and consistency collapse across many task types in the same session, the player may need a readiness fix before adding more scenario volume.
why: Sleep, movement, and recovery affect visual processing, focus, and stable execution more than players often admit.
A low-readiness session can look like a mechanical regression even when the real issue is recovery.
actions: If the whole block feels unusually slow or inconsistent, shorten the volume and protect quality instead of forcing a normal full session.
Build one pre-session reset habit such as a short walk, hydration, or light movement before the hard block.
Track whether poor sleep and poor consistency line up before assuming the scenario plan is the only problem.
avoid: Do not interpret every low-readiness day as proof that the routine stopped working.
